title: Authentication handlers and policies
summary: Plug your own scheme into ASP.NET Core with AuthenticationHandler, then protect endpoints with RequireAuthorization, roles and policies.

steps.title: Your own authentication scheme
body: The authentication system is pluggable. `AddJwtBearer` is just one **handler**; you can write another by deriving from `AuthenticationHandler<TOptions>`, which is in the framework itself:
class HsBearerHandler(IOptionsMonitor<AuthenticationSchemeOptions> options, ILoggerFactory logger, UrlEncoder encoder)
- `NoResult()`: no credentials. The user is anonymous; endpoints that need a user will **challenge**.
- `Fail(...)`: bad credentials. Also anonymous, and logged.

The base class answers a challenge with `401` and a forbid with `403`. Override `HandleChallengeAsync` to add the `WWW-Authenticate` header. The same pattern is used in real code for API keys, HMAC-signed webhooks and mutual TLS.

steps.title: Requiring authorization
body: With authentication registered, endpoints declare what they need, and `UseAuthorization` enforces it:
// MVC controllers use attributes for the same thing:
**Policies** are named rule sets, registered once:
// deny by default: every endpoint without its own rule needs a signed-in user
An anonymous caller that fails a policy is **challenged** (`401`); a signed-in caller that fails it is **forbidden** (`403`). You get the right status code for free.

steps.prompt: Match each requirement to its policy builder call.
pairs: Has the `tasks:write` scope in a space-separated claim
steps.explain: `RequireClaim("scope", "tasks:write")` would compare the *whole* claim value, so it fails for `"tasks:read tasks:write"`. Space-separated scopes need an assertion (or a custom requirement).

steps.prompt: An anonymous request hits an endpoint with `.RequireAuthorization("Admin")`. What status comes back?
options: 401, because there is no user to evaluate yet: the scheme is challenged

steps.prompt: Register the scheme and a role policy.

A team adds `options.FallbackPolicy = new AuthorizationPolicyBuilder().RequireAuthenticatedUser().Build();`. A developer then adds `app.MapGet("/reports", ...)` and forgets any authorization call. What happens to anonymous callers?
options: They get 401: endpoints without their own rule fall back to requiring a signed-in user
They get the reports: no rule means open
steps.explain: That is deny by default. Public endpoints must opt out explicitly with `AllowAnonymous()`.

steps.title: Handler and policies
prompt: The starter contains a complete `HsBearerHandler` and the `TokenValidator` (with `ToPrincipal`), and five endpoints with no protection. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.
1. Register the `"Bearer"` scheme with `HsBearerHandler` as the default, and add `UseAuthentication()` and `UseAuthorization()`.
2. Add policies: `"Admin"` (role `admin`), `"TasksRead"` and `"TasksWrite"` (the space-separated `scope` claim contains `tasks:read` / `tasks:write`, exactly).
3. Protect: `/me` any signed-in user, `GET /tasks` `TasksRead`, `POST /tasks` `TasksWrite`, `DELETE /admin/tasks/{id}` `Admin`. `/public` stays open.

// Checks alg, signature, exp (30 s skew), iss and aud. Returns the payload JSON, or null.
public static string? ValidatePayload(string token, long now)
if (!header.RootElement.TryGetProperty("alg", out var alg) || alg.GetString() != "HS256") return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("exp", out var exp) || exp.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Number || now >= exp.GetInt64() + 30) return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("iss", out var iss) || iss.GetString() != "https://auth.dojo") return null;
if (!p.TryGetProperty("aud", out var aud) || aud.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String || aud.GetString() != "tasks-api") return null;

static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Authentication could be checked", async () =>
Dojo.Eq("GET /public is open", "hello", await DojoWeb.Text(await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/public", null)));
var anon = await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", null);
DojoWeb.Status("GET /me anonymously gets 401", 401, anon);
Dojo.Check("with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer", DojoAuth.Challenge(anon).StartsWith("Bearer"), DojoAuth.Challenge(anon));
DojoWeb.Status("GET /me with an expired token gets 401", 401, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", DojoAuth.For("ada", exp: 1000000000)));
var me = await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", DojoAuth.For("ada"));
DojoWeb.Status("GET /me with a good token gets 200", 200, me);
Dojo.Eq("and the name is sub", "ada", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(me), "sub"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Policies could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("GET /tasks anonymously gets 401", 401, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/tasks", null));
DojoWeb.Status("GET /tasks without tasks:read gets 403", 403, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/tasks", DojoAuth.For("ada", scope: "profile")));
DojoWeb.Status("GET /tasks with tasks:read gets 200", 200, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Get, "/tasks", DojoAuth.For("ada", scope: "tasks:read")));
DojoWeb.Status("POST /tasks with only tasks:read gets 403", 403, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Post, "/tasks", DojoAuth.For("ada", scope: "tasks:read")));
DojoWeb.Status("POST /tasks with tasks:read tasks:write gets 201", 201, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Post, "/tasks", DojoAuth.For("ada", scope: "tasks:read tasks:write")));
DojoWeb.Status("a scope prefix doesn't count (tasks:writer)", 403, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Post, "/tasks", DojoAuth.For("ada", scope: "tasks:writer")));
DojoWeb.Status("DELETE /admin/tasks/1 anonymously gets 401", 401, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Delete, "/admin/tasks/1", null));
DojoWeb.Status("DELETE /admin/tasks/1 as a user gets 403", 403, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Delete, "/admin/tasks/1", DojoAuth.For("ada", "[\"user\"]")));
DojoWeb.Status("DELETE /admin/tasks/1 as an admin gets 204", 204, await DojoAuth.Send(http, HttpMethod.Delete, "/admin/tasks/1", DojoAuth.For("root", "[\"admin\"]")));
static class DojoAuth
static string B64(byte[] d) => Convert.ToBase64String(d).TrimEnd('=').Replace('+', '-').Replace('/', '_');
static string B64(string s) => B64(System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(s));
public static string Sign(string payload, string? key = null, string header = "{\"alg\":\"HS256\",\"typ\":\"JWT\"}")
var input = B64(header) + "." + B64(payload);
var k = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(key ?? "aspnet-demo-signing-key-0123456789ab");
return input + "." + B64(System.Security.Cryptography.HMACSHA256.HashData(k, System.Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(input)));
// A valid token for tasks-api that expires in 2100.
public static string For(string sub, string roles = "[]", string scope = "", long exp = 4102444800) =>
Sign("{\"iss\":\"https://auth.dojo\",\"aud\":\"tasks-api\",\"sub\":\"" + sub + "\",\"role\":" + roles + ",\"scope\":\"" + scope + "\",\"exp\":" + exp + "}");
public static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient http, HttpMethod method, string url, string? token, string scheme = "Bearer")
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(method, url);
if (token is not null) msg.Headers.TryAddWithoutValidation("Authorization", scheme + " " + token);
return http.SendAsync(msg);
public static string Challenge(HttpResponseMessage r) =>
r.Headers.WwwAuthenticate.Count > 0 ? string.Join(",", r.Headers.WwwAuthenticate) : "";
